'''''Persicaria minor''''' is species of herb in the family [[Polygonaceae]]. Common names include '''pygmy smartweed''',<ref name=PLANTS>{{PLANTS | symbol = POMI21 | taxon = Polygonum minus | access-date = 12 April 2021}}</ref> '''small water pepper''' and '''swamp willow weed'''.<ref name=EPPO>{{cite web | title = ''Persicaria minor'' | url = https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/POLMI | publisher = [[European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization]] (EPPO) | access-date = 12 April 2021}}</ref> This herb is native to Asia, but distributed widely in Europe and Australia.<ref>{{ cite web | title=Persicaria minor (Huds.) Opiz | url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/persicaria/minor/ | publisher=New England Wild Flower Society | access-date=2017-03-28 }}</ref> It is used in [[South East Asia]]n cooking.

==Description==
''Persicaria minor'' is native to South East Asia, including Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia.<ref name="ulam">{{ cite book | date=2010 | first=W.E | last=Wan Hassan | title=Ulam: Salad Herbs of Malaysia | publisher=Masbe | isbn=9789834466404 | pages=190–191 }}</ref> It grows wild in cooler highlands, but is also found in wet lowland areas near rivers, ditches, and canals. It is a creeping plant with slender stems, and grows upright to a height of 1 to 1.5 meters. The creeping stem is green with reddish tinge, is cylindrical in shape, and has short nodes about 9 mm apart. Its leaves are long and narrowly tapering, alternately arranged, and green with short, reddish petioles. Its flowers are minute, pale violet, and are 12 to 15 cm long.<ref name="HerbsOfMalaysia">{{ cite book | first1=Joseph | last1=Samy | first2=M.| last2=Sugumaran | first3=Kate | last3=Lee | date=2005 | title=Herbs of Malaysia | publisher=Times Editions - Marshall Cavendish | isbn=9833001793 | pages=198–199 }}</ref>

==Uses==
''Persicaria minor'' is an edible, aromatic herb. In Malaysia and Indonesia it has the common name "kesum", and its shoots and young leaves are eaten raw as part of salad ([[ulam (salad)|ulam]]); used as an aroma spice additive in peppery dishes such as [[laksa]], [[nasi kerabu]], [[asam pedas]] and [[tom yam]]; used as tea leaves; and used for topical applications in traditional medicine.<ref>{{ cite web| first=Chris | last=Kilham | date=2017-02-26 | title=South Asian herb dubbed 'smart weed' | url=https://www.foxnews.com/health/south-asian-herb-dubbed-smart-weed | publisher=FoxNews.com | access-date=2017-08-11 }}</ref><ref>{{ cite journal| first1=Nur Huda | last1=Faujan| first2=Noriham |last2=Abdullah|first3=Norrakiah |last3=Abdullah Sani|first4=Abdul |last4=Salam Babji|title=Antioxidative activities of water extracts of some Malaysian herbs| journal=ASEAN Food Journal| year=2007| volume=14| issue=1| pages=61–68 }}</ref> Its oil has been used for aromatherapy and in treatments for dandruff. In Malaysian traditional medicine, ''P. minor'' has been used in post-natal tonics and for treatment of digestion.<ref name="HerbsOfMalaysia" />

==Composition==
''P. minor'' has high content of dietary fiber, thiamine, carbohydrate, protein and minerals.<ref name="ulam" /> It is also rich in calcium, potassium, vitamin A and vitamin C, which reportedly gives it a high level of antioxidant properties.<ref name="HerbsOfMalaysia" /><ref name="ulam" /> Other constituents include quercetin,<ref>{{ cite book | title=The Wonders of Kesum | editor1=Suzana Shahar | editor2=Hanis Mastura Yahya | editor3=Annie George | publisher=University Kebangsaan Malaysia Press | year=2021 | pages=25 }}</ref> quercetin-3-glucuronide, myricetin, apigetrin, hyperoside and astragalin.<ref>{{ cite journal| last1=Abdullah| first1=Mohamad Zakkirun| last2=Mohd Ali| first2=Johari| last3=Abolmaesoomi| first3=Mitra| last4=Abdul-Rahman| first4=Puteri Shafinaz| last5=Hashim| first5=Onn Haji|title=Anti-Proliferative, in Vitro Antioxidant, and Cellular Antioxidant Activities of the Leaf Extracts from Polygonum Minus Huds: Effects of Solvent Polarity | journal=International Journal of Food Properties| year=2017| volume=20| issue=20| pages=S846–S862 |doi=10.1080/10942912.2017.1315591 | doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="lau" />
